subject: Optimize Toolkit pricing & bundling — quantization + volume discount discussion
messages:
From: Lisa Cheng <finance@finopsai.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, procurement@finopsai.com
Date: Tue, 18 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Optimize Toolkit — request for bundle & discount details

Hi Sean / Marissa,

Thanks again for the demo last week. We liked the Optimize toolkit recommendations around batching and prefix caching — looks promising for our ingestion-heavy workload. Before we move procurement forward, finance needs a clearer pricing picture for the toolkit add-on and any discounts tied to committed usage. A few concrete asks: 

- Can you break out the pricing for: automated batching suggestions, prefix/KV cache credits, and quantization consultancy (one-time)?
- Do you offer volume tiers or committed monthly credits that reduce per-token cost when batching/cache is used?
- We run 25M generated tokens/month today with a 60/40 mix of hosted vs dedicated endpoints in prod. What's a plausible discount if we commit 12 months at 50M tokens/month and adopt 8-bit quantization on eligible models?

Also, procurement may want the mutual action plan and a short SOW for the quantization pilot. Please attach any benchmark artifacts you used in the demo.

Thanks,
Lisa Cheng
VP Finance | FinOpsAI
finance@finopsai.com

(Attachment: sample_contracts.pdf)
From: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>
To: Lisa Cheng <finance@finopsai.com>, Rahul Mehta <cto@finopsai.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 18 Aug 2026 11:05:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Optimize Toolkit — request for bundle & discount details

Hi Lisa / Rahul — great to connect.

Short answers up front, followed by a suggested approach and a 3-point MAP: 

1) Pricing breakout (headline):
- Optimize Toolkit subscription: $2,500 / month (includes console insights + per-route batching recommendations)
- Cache credits: billed as storage-credit units; baseline 10k credits/month included. Additional credits: $0.0012 / credit.
- Quantization advisory (one-time): $18,000 for model analysis, quantization testing, and a deployment-ready quantized variant (includes up to 2 models).

2) Volume / commitment discounts:
- 12-month prepaid commitments: tiered discounts on per-token usage (hosted/dedicated): 10% at 25M/mo, 18% at 50M/mo, 25% at 100M/mo.
- Additional discount for enabling quantization on eligible models: one-time 5% uplift on the committed discount for the first 6 months (to reflect accelerated cost-savings).

3) Plausible economics for your example (50M tokens/mo, 12mo commit, quantization enabled on eligible models):
- Baseline per-token unit (hosted generation): $0.0008 / token. With 18% commit discount -> $0.000656 / token.
- With the 5% quantization uplift applied to the discount -> effective rate approx $0.000623 / token.
- Estimated annual savings vs no-commit baseline: ~22% (token + quantization + cache effects not yet included).

Suggested plan / MAP:
A) PoC & Benchmarks (2 weeks): we run quant-benchmarks on one production model, measure latency/cost delta with 8-bit quant, and scope caching opportunities (deliverable: quant-benchmarks-2026.csv).
B) Pilot (4–6 weeks): enable Optimize Toolkit rules for batching and prefix caching on a subset of traffic; measure realized token reduction and tail latency.
C) Roll & Commit: finalize commitment and apply credit tiers + discount. Provide SOW for quantization work and transition plan for dedicated endpoints if needed.

I attached a short pricing brief, the benchmark CSV from the demo, and a draft MAP doc (RDW-FinOpsAI-MAP-v1.docx). If procurement prefers a worksheet with line items, we can export a quote.

If this looks reasonable, I can follow with a formal quote and SOW for the quantization advisory.

Cheers,
Sean Gallagher
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
sean_gallagher@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0192

(Attachments: Optimize_Toolkit_Pricing_Brief.pdf, quant-benchmarks-2026.csv, RDW-FinOpsAI-MAP-v1.docx)
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 18 Aug 2026 12:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Internal: recommended concession and approval path

Sean / Karthik — quick internal note before we send a formal quote to FinOpsAI.

Context: Lisa asked for a clearer breakdown and a discount question for a 12-month 50M/mo commit. Procurement will push for a deeper discount and proof of quantization safety.

Recommended commercial approach: 
- Offer a structured discount ladder with clear guardrails: 18% at 50M/mo, but include a 9-month step-down clause if actual usage < 40M/mo for two consecutive months. This protects us vs overcommitment.
- Include two complimentary quantization lab hours (up to 8 engineer-hours) and apply a $6k credit toward the one-time quant advisory if they sign within 30 days. This makes the advisory feel less front-loaded.
- Add 3 months of expanded cache credits (double baseline) as an onboarding incentive to demonstrate immediate cost savings; tie the cache overage rate to usage so they don't surprise procurement.
- Approvals needed: discount authority up to 20% (I can approve) and any greater needs to route to RevOps. Karthik, can you confirm we have capacity to run the PoC in the last week of Aug?

If agreed, Sean — I recommend we send a two-page commercial term sheet plus the MAP and highlight the commit protections. Keep technical claims conservative: provide measured results from the PoC, don't promise blanket 8-bit parity.

—Marissa
Marissa Cole
Head of Solutions | Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.ai
From: Rahul Mehta <cto@finopsai.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: Lisa Cheng <finance@finopsai.com>, procurement@finopsai.com
Date: Thu, 20 Aug 2026 15:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Optimize Toolkit — request for bundle & discount details

Thanks, Sean — this is helpful. A couple quick clarifications from our side before procurement drafts the PO: 

1) The quantization uplift to the committed discount (the +5%) — is that applied to the discount percentage (i.e., 18% -> 18.9%), or to the effective per-token price after the discount? We prefer clarity on the math.
2) For the cache credits: can you provide a worked example showing how cache credits translate to monthly $ savings given our traffic profile (25M gen tokens/mo today; we expect 2–3x reduction on cached prefixes for queries that match historical prompts)?
3) Can the PoC include a short acceptance criteria doc so procurement can justify the SOW spend?

If you can send the worked example and a revised commercial two-pager with the concession language Marissa suggested, we can move to a redline-ready term sheet. Otherwise procurement will come back with multiple discount asks.

Regards,
Rahul Mehta
CTO | FinOpsAI
cto@finopsai.com
